transcript:
Header: 2026-10-02 14:00 PDT | Duration: 52 mins | Recording: Yes
Attendees: Jordan, Rina, Marco (Redwood) / Priya, Liam, Diane, Owen, Sara (Mariner)

Summary: quick sync to validate rollback playbook after last week's kernel upgrade trial; align on dry-run window, and confirm who owns which steps during an emergency fallback to hosted variant. Brief perf checks on quantized variant and notes on egress shaping.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone uh thanks for joining on time um we'll keep this tight 50 minutes ish; goal is to finalize who's owning the rollback steps and lock a dry run window.
[00:18] Priya: thanks Jordan, appreciate it. quick context: last week our staging saw a 2x p99 spike during long sequences after the kernel patch. we reverted but want a better playbook.
[00:33] Rina: yeah and we saw that the quantized kernels had a slightly different cache warmup pattern, so initial tokens spiked. that's what we want to mitigate w/ prefix caching and a quick fallback to hosted.
[00:49] Liam: just to add, the p99 spike actually correlated with concurrent sessions hitting a specific route that uses longer sequences, so it's kinda workload-shape dependent.
[01:07] Marco: (note: ran a quick repro) we triggered similar behavior locally when KV cache was cold and batching kicked in. there was a short window where latency jumped.
[01:22] Owen: can you restate what the recommended threshold is for circuit-breaker? we discussed 500ms but not sure if that covers our SLA.
[01:32] Jordan: good question — Redwood suggests a rolling p99 threshold of 400–600ms for this workload during shipping, but the circuit-breaker policy should include token-rate too; we'll propose a policy in the doc.
[01:47] Diane: for compliance we need audit logs retained for 90 days and we need to ensure the rollback doesn't bypass log collection; is that covered?
[01:56] Rina: yes — rollback triggers an event that still ships telemetry to your on-prem collector; we haven't changed the retention semantics. we'll share the telemetry flow diagram.
[02:10] Sara: quick scheduling note — our engineering freeze is 10/10 so dry-run must be before then ideally.

[02:28] Jordan: ok next let's walk through the playbook steps we drafted. Marco, can you do the read-through?
[02:35] Marco: sure. step one: detect and alert — headroom monitor hits threshold; step two: automatic fallback to hosted variant for affected model route; step three: progressively scale down to previous kernel; step four: post-mortem and patch cadence.
[02:51] Priya: for step two, hosted fallback means traffic egresses to Redwood hosted API, correct? any egress setup needed for us?
[03:01] Rina: correct. you'll need outbound access to redwood-hosted endpoints and a short-lived behavior change (we route with a canary header). Owen, does NetOps allow that?
[03:12] Owen: we can open outbound but we need IP ranges and FQDNs. we prefer allowlists not broad 0.0.0.0/0.
[03:20] Jordan: we'll provide CIDR lists and DNS names; we'll also provide a signed PSK handshake doc for the mutual TLS + PSK if you prefer to authenticate before egress.
[03:31] Diane: PSK is okay but we need HSM/KMS proof that keys are rotated every 90 days. is Redwood supporting key rotation?
[03:40] Rina: yes, we support KMS integrations and key rotation automation; we'll include a sample rotation config in the security appendix.

[03:55] Liam: about the rollback timeline — if we detect the spike, what is the expected time to failover to hosted? 30s? 2 minutes?
[04:04] Marco: with the circuit-breaker and prefix caching warm paths it's usually sub-2min, oftentimes under 45s, but depends on KV cache coldness and batch drains.
[04:17] Priya: we need that number in an SLA-style sentence for ops.

[04:25] Jordan: noted, we'll craft a short SLO blurb: target failover 90th percentile under 60s for similar workloads; worst-case documented.

[04:40] Owen: firewall/QoS — we plan to shape egress so that fallback traffic doesn't saturate our egress pipe. what controls do you recommend?
[04:50] Rina: a few knobs — per-route rate limiting at your edge, token-aware shapers, and also Redwood supports burst profiles so you can limit sustained bandwidth and allow short bursts. we'll share recommended defaults.

[05:05] Sara: can we talk about the dry-run? we want a rehearsal where we simulate kernel degradation and trigger the playbook. what does Redwood need from us?
[05:16] Marco: we'll need a staging endpoint with identical routing rules and an agreed maintenance window. we'll push a canary kernel that increases simulated token processing time by 30% and observe.
[05:28] Liam: we can do that if it doesn't affect other teams; we'll schedule a 2-hour window.

[05:40] Jordan: perfect. Rina, you had some quick perf notes from yesterday's microbenchmark?
[05:46] Rina: yes — I ran quantized-kernel A vs A' on a V100-equivalent and saw average token latency 1.12x but tail increased 1.9x for sequences >1k tokens. it suggests cache warm-up and kernel pathing issues. attaching TL;DR: recommend early prefix caching and a small initial batch size during recovery.
[06:08] Priya: is that something we can toggle at runtime? we want to avoid restarts.
[06:14] Rina: prefix caching and dynamic batch sizing are runtime toggles for Redwood private runtime; no full restart required, though the kernel change itself obviously requires planned deployment.

[06:30] Owen: question on metrics — will the fallback to hosted preserve trace IDs and user attribution for billing and logs? we need to reconcile logs across systems.
[06:40] Marco: yes we inject a correlation header X-Redwood-Correlation that you can map back; we also support a mapping file export so you can join traces in your SIEM.
[06:51] Diane: make sure that mapping file doesn't leak PII — we only want pseudonymous IDs.
[06:56] Jordan: agreed, we'll send sample mappings — no actual PII.

[07:05] (brief cross-talk; hands being shuffled)
[07:18] Sara: ok timeline recap from our side: dry-run before 10/10, compliance review by 10/09, and rollback doc finalized by 10/05.
[07:30] Jordan: yep. anything else on the runbook itself?
[07:36] Priya: add an explicit step for feature-flag toggles and owner escalation tree for PagerDuty. last time pager escalation was ambiguous.
[07:47] Rina: we'll add a matrix: condition -> immediate action -> owner -> fallback route.

[07:58] Liam: small ask — can the SE run an experiment showing payload-batching disabled vs enabled with our typical batch mix? it helps us decide the circuit breaker thresholds.
[08:08] Rina: yes I'll run a targeted experiment; need your sample trace or synthetic generator.
[08:15] Liam: I'll push a sanitized trace dump to the shared folder by EOD.

[08:22] Jordan: perfect. Next section: security gating for on-prem log ingestion during fallback. Diane?
[08:29] Diane: important that fallback doesn't invoice any extra ingestion to our external SIEM without approvals — we need cost visibility. also need to ensure hashes rather than raw data.
[08:39] Marco: we support publish-subscribe to your on-prem collector and can throttle log volumes; also we'll provide hash-only options for sensitive fields.

[08:50] Owen: technical note — for mutual TLS we prefer a two-way handshake with cert pinning for Redwood nodes. is that supported for hosted fallback?
[08:59] Jordan: yes, we can do mTLS and cert pinning; PSK is an alternative for quicker installs. we'll document both.

[09:12] Sara: stakeholder comms — we'll need a short blurb for executives describing risk and mitigation. can Redwood draft a 1-pager?
[09:19] Jordan: yes, we'll create a one-pager with timeline and residual risk, plus the runbook link.

[09:28] (silence, typing)
[09:40] Priya: another edge case — what if the hosted variant is also under load? fallback to hosted sounds good but if the hosted variant is congested how do we mitigate?
[09:50] Marco: we have a tiered fallback: first try a compatible local quantized variant with more conservative batch settings; if that fails, route a fraction of traffic to hosted while shedding low-priority requests; we also have rate-limited queued retries.
[10:08] Liam: can we get a short diagram of that flow?
[10:12] Jordan: will include a diagram in the playbook.

[10:20] Rina: last technical note — kernel rollback can be automated via our orchestrator but we recommend manual confirmation for production. automation for staging is fine.
[10:32] Priya: agreed, manual confirm in prod.

[10:40] Jordan: ok wrap up checklist: Jordan to upload doc; Rina to run microbench and Marco to prepare fallback flow diagram; Owen to confirm firewall window; Diane to validate compliance artifacts; Liam to push sample traces; Sara to book dry-run.
[10:55] Priya: thanks all, that covers it.
[11:00] Jordan: great — we'll target those dates in next steps. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References & links: shared drive: https://redwood.company/shared/mariner/rollback-playbook-v2 (doc), quick microbenchmark sheet: https://redwood.company/tmp/mariner-bench-20261001.csv
